description: The Australian Bureau of Meteorology gives access to national water data through two linked services. The Australian Water Data Service, read on 2026-09-28, is an ArcGIS-based portal for the spatial water data, interfaces for programs and maps behind the Bureau's water information, searchable by groundwater, surface water, water storage and flood. Its applications include the Geofabric, which registers how rivers, water bodies, aquifers and monitoring points connect; the Groundwater Explorer, with more than 870,000 bore locations, bore logs, groundwater levels and salinity; an atlas of groundwater-dependent ecosystems with downloads; a water storage dashboard by state, capital city, drainage division, major supply system and individual storage, compared over the past day to year; and the Australian Water Outlook, giving soil moisture, runoff, evaporation and rainfall as daily history, one-to-three-month forecasts and long-term projections. Time series from monitoring stations sit in Water Data Online, whose page says it provides public access to Australia's water data. Coverage is Australia. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC-BY-4.0 unless otherwise noted (Bureau of Meteorology copyright page); some material under data licence agreements. Access is free of charge. Caveats: the Water Data Online station interface itself did not load in the cloud session. It supports hazard and capacity studies, such as tracking storage levels of city supply systems during drought. Related records: the Bureau's urban water performance report and Murray-Darling Basin portal.
